shared_elements: low-relief carving on a flat face
justification: Both are tall upright limestone-coloured slabs bearing shallow relief organised into stacked horizontal registers, with a band of repeated small motifs crossing the upper area and profile creature forms below. However, A's surface is densely packed edge to edge with intricate, interlocking anthropomorphic and glyph-like detail carved in fine crisp line, while B leaves wide blank ground around a few large, simply outlined animal shapes with soft rounded modelling; the two also differ entirely in setting and in the shape of the stone (B has a broad projecting head-like top).
